query_text: Plan a seven-day trip in China.

parts.text:
A seven-day trip to China is the perfect amount of time to experience the country’s dramatic contrast between ancient imperial history and futuristic modernity. 

The ultimate first-timer itinerary is the **"Golden Route" connecting Beijing (the imperial capital) and Shanghai (the modern metropolis)**. These cities are seamlessly connected by a state-of-the-art, 4.5-hour high-speed train.

---

### **The Itinerary: Beijing & Shanghai (7 Days)**

#### **Day 1: Arrival in Beijing & Ancient Hutongs**
*   **Morning/Afternoon:** Arrive at Beijing Capital (PEK) or Daxing (PKX) Airport. Check into your hotel (staying in the central *Dongcheng* district near Wangfujing or Houhai is highly recommended). 
*   **Late Afternoon:** Explore Beijing’s **Hutongs**—narrow, centuries-old alleyways lined with traditional courtyard homes. Walk through the trendy **Wudaoying Hutong** or **Nanluoguxiang** for boutique shops and cafes.
*   **Evening:** Walk around the scenic **Houhai Lake** as the waterfront bars light up. 
*   **Dinner:** Enjoy an authentic welcome dinner of crispy **Peking Roasted Duck** at a local favorite like *Siji Minfu* or *Da Dong*.

#### **Day 2: The Heart of Imperial Beijing**
*   **Morning:** Visit **Tiananmen Square**, the symbolic heart of China, then walk through the Meridian Gate into the majestic **Forbidden City** (Imperial Palace). *Note: You must book these tickets up to 7 days in advance online.*
*   **Lunch:** Grab hand-pulled noodles or dumplings nearby.
*   **Afternoon:** Climb the hill in **Jingshan Park** (directly behind the Forbidden City exit) for an incredible 360-degree panoramic view of the palace's golden roofs. Afterward, take a taxi to the **Temple of Heaven**, a masterpiece of Ming Dynasty architecture where emperors once prayed for good harvests.
*   **Evening:** Walk through **Wangfujing Pedestrian Street** for shopping and modern food stalls.

#### **Day 3: The Great Wall & Olympic Legacy**
*   **Morning:** Take a private car or express bus to the **Mutianyu section of the Great Wall** (about 1.5 hours from downtown). It is less crowded and more scenic than Badaling. Take the cable car up to the wall, hike along the ancient watchtowers, and ride the thrilling **toboggan slide** back down to the bottom.
*   **Afternoon:** On your way back to the city, stop at the **Olympic Park** to photograph the iconic **Bird’s Nest** (National Stadium) and **Water Cube** (National Aquatics Center).
*   **Evening:** Head to **Sanlitun**, Beijing’s trendy, international district, for dinner and craft beer.

#### **Day 4: Summer Palace & Bullet Train to Shanghai**
*   **Morning:** Explore the tranquil **Summer Palace** (Yiheyuan), the imperial family's lakeside retreat. Walk along the record-breaking Long Corridor and admire the marble boat.
*   **Afternoon:** Board the state-of-the-art **Fuxing High-Speed Train** from Beijing South to Shanghai Hongqiao (approx. 4.5 hours, traveling at speeds up to 350 km/h). Watch the Chinese countryside fly past your window.
*   **Evening:** Arrive in Shanghai and check into your hotel (the *Huangpu* district is highly recommended). Head straight to **The Bund** to see the famous, breathtaking neon skyline of Pudong reflecting across the Huangpu River.

#### **Day 5: Futuristic Skylines & French Concession**
*   **Morning:** Step back in time at **Yu Garden** (a classic 16th-century Chinese garden) and explore the bustling traditional bazaar surrounding it.
*   **Afternoon:** Contrast the old with the new. Take the ferry or metro across the river to Lujiazui (Pudong) and ascend to the observation deck of the **Shanghai Tower** (the world’s second-tallest building) for birds-eye views. 
*   **Later:** Walk through the historic, leafy streets of the **Former French Concession**. Explore the shikumen-style stone alleyways of **Tianzifang** or **Xintiandi**, packed with cafes and art galleries.
*   **Evening:** Walk and shop down **Nanjing Road**, Shanghai's premier shopping street.

#### **Day 6: Water Town Day Trip**
*   **Morning/Afternoon:** Escaping the steel-and-glass towers, take a day trip to an ancient water town. 
    *   *Option A:* Take Shanghai Metro Line 17 to **Zhujiajiao Water Town** (1 hour from downtown).
    *   *Option B:* Take a quick 30-minute bullet train to **Suzhou**, the "Venice of the East," to visit UNESCO-listed classical gardens and ride a hand-paddled gondola through the canals.
*   **Evening:** Return to Shanghai. Celebrate your last night with a cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the Bund, or enjoy live jazz at the famous Peace Hotel.

#### **Day 7: Art & High-Tech Departure**
*   **Morning:** Visit the spectacular **Shanghai Museum** (either the classic People's Square branch or the massive new East Branch) to view ancient Chinese bronzes, ceramics, and calligraphy.
*   **Afternoon:** Do any last-minute shopping. Head to Pudong International Airport (PVG) using the **Maglev Train**—the world's fastest commercial levitating train, reaching speeds up to 430 km/h—and catch your flight home.

---

### **Crucial Travel Tips for China**

#### **1. Visa-Free Entry**
China has significantly expanded its unilateral visa-free entry policies. 
*   **30-Day Visa-Free Stay:** Ordinary passport holders from **most European countries** (including the UK, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, Poland, Norway, and more), **Australia, New Zealand, Japan, and South Korea** can enter China completely visa-free for up to 30 days for tourism. This policy is currently active.
*   **144-Hour Transit Visa-Free:** If you are from a country not on the unilateral list (like the United States or Canada), you can still visit visa-free for up to 6 days (144 hours) if you are transiting through China to a third country (e.g., USA $\rightarrow$ Beijing $\rightarrow$ Tokyo).

#### **2. Payments (China is Cashless)**
Practically no one uses cash or physical credit cards in China. 
*   **Before you fly:** Download **Alipay** and **WeChat**. 
*   You can easily verify your identity with your passport and link your international Visa, Mastercard, or Discover card directly to these apps. U.S. users can also link PayPal via WeChat Pay.
*   You will pay by scanning QR codes for everything from street-food dumplings to subway tickets. Note that a 3% fee applies to transactions over 200 RMB (~$28 USD).

#### **3. Internet & Bypassing the Firewall**
To access Western apps (Google, Instagram, WhatsApp, YouTube, etc.), the standard internet will block them.
*   **The Best Solution:** Purchase an **eSIM with data roaming** (such as Airalo, Nomad, or Holafly) before you arrive. Because it runs on international roaming, it automatically bypasses China's Great Firewall without needing a VPN.
*   **Alternative:** If you use local Wi-Fi, you must download a high-quality VPN (like Astrill VPN) *before* you land in China, as app stores will block VPN downloads once you are in the country.

#### **4. Essential Apps to Download**
*   **Didi:** The Chinese equivalent of Uber (conveniently built directly inside the Alipay app as a mini-program).
*   **Apple Maps or Gaode Maps:** Google Maps is highly inaccurate in China. Apple Maps works perfectly, or you can use Gaode (Amap) if you can navigate basic Chinese.
*   **Google Translate / Baidu Translate:** For instant camera-translation of menus and signs.
